item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00388","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C19","C03","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C19","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C19 is the immediately preceding United Givers Fund memorandum and supplies the child’s specific structure and much of its substance: the same National Capital Area campaign, the same bundled organizations, its position as the first of two campaigns under the approved Federal fund-raising policy, appointment of a Cabinet officer as Government Unit chairman, participation by civilian and military personnel, and a closing appeal to make the campaign an outstanding success. C03 and C06 share narrower campaign formulas, but neither approaches C19’s concrete correspondence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"This fall marks the second annual United Givers Fund Campaign held in the National Capital Area. In this great appeal are included the needs of the Community Chest-Red Feather agencies, all of the local chapters of the American Red Cross, the USO and certain national health agencies","parent_excerpt":"Next Fall, in the National Capital Area, the \"United Givers Fund\" campaign will unite for the first time the more than one hundred Red Feather agencies of the six local Community Chests, all of the American National Red Cross local chapters, the USO-USO Camp Shows and certain national health agencies.","explanation":"The child updates the inaugural 1956 campaign into its second annual iteration while retaining the same distinctive aggregation of participating organizations."},{"child_excerpt":"The United Givers Fund Campaign is the first of two campaigns conducted among us each year under the approved Federal Service fund-raising policy.","parent_excerpt":"It is also the first of two campaigns in the Greater Washington Metropolitan Area to be conducted in Federal offices under the new approved Federal service fund-raising policy.","explanation":"This is close, distinctive shared language describing the campaign’s exact administrative position under the federal fund-raising policy."},{"child_excerpt":"During this campaign, all civilian and military personnel serving here are given an opportunity to contribute","parent_excerpt":"Every Government official, employee and all military personnel on duty in the National Capital Area will be given the opportunity to contribute voluntarily","explanation":"The child closely reworks the parent’s participation provision for federal civilian and military personnel."},{"child_excerpt":"The Honorable Fred A. Seaton, Secretary of the Interior, has kindly consented to act as Chairman of the Government Unit of the United Givers Fund Campaign. I know everyone will want to join him in making this 1957 fund-raising effort an outstanding success.","parent_excerpt":"I appoint the Honorable James P. Mitchell, Secretary of Labor, to act as Chairman of the 1956 Government Unit of the United Givers Fund in this first appeal under the new Federal program. ... I should like all Federal employees to join with me in making this community fund-raising effort an outstanding success.","explanation":"The same machinery and closing appeal are retained, with the chairman, year, and phrasing adjusted."}]}
